# Saccavibhaṅga Sutta (MN 141 (PTS MN iii 248))

**ID:** MN 141 (PTS MN iii 248)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Saccavibhaṅga Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** The Analysis of the Truths  
**PTS:** MN iii 248  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

This exposition combines brief definitions with word-by-word exegeses for the first truth (*dukkha*) and the fourth truth (the noble eightfold path), while retaining standard formulaic summaries for the origin and cessation of suffering [Anālayo, Dawn of Abhidharma].

Furthermore, comparative analysis indicates that an *Ekottarika-āgama* parallel lacks the qualification "noble" (*ariya*), referring simply to "four truths" and highlighting the gradual development of doctrinal terminology [Shulman 2014].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: EA 27.1; MA 31 分別聖諦; T 32 四諦
- Resembling parallels: DN 22 (PTS DN ii 290) Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta; EA 12.1 ?; MA 98 念處; MN 10 (PTS MN i 55) Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta; SHT Sutta 11

**Sources**

- [Anālayo, Dawn of Abhidharma] Anālayo, The Dawn of Abhidharma — Exposition structure of the first and fourth truths versus second and third, relation to DN 22, and late developmental layers.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (1983) — Location in Vibhaṅgavagga, commentarial character on the first sermon, possible interpolation, relation to DN 22 and Vibhaṅga Suttanta-bhājanīya.
- [Shulman 2014] Eviatar Shulman, Rethinking the Buddha (2014) — Combination of texts in DN 22 and the absence of 'ariya' in the Ekottarika-āgama parallel.
